about: One entry per release tag. kind: "fix" (doesn't change how Charles trades) or "rule" (does, or might). The dashboard's Updates card and charles-update read this; see docs/releases.md.

notes: A server made by "Set it up for me" has a key page: paste your Alpaca paper keys on a page on your own server, press Start Charles, and your dashboard opens, logged in. No terminal needed. The keys go only from your browser to your server, and the page works once, for a day, only over HTTPS.
A free install has no key page and works as before: nano, charles-start, charles-login.
The dashboard login now renews itself while you use it, so a browser you open at least once every 30 days stays logged in.
How Charles trades doesn't change.
The dashboard's chat (Ask Charles) is gone, and so is the Anthropic key it needed. The sliders, presets, Copy and Undo work as before, and how Charles trades doesn't change.

To change Charles in plain words, use Claude Code on your own server. Your Charles folder now has a CLAUDE.md that tells Claude Code how Charles fits together and what's safe to change. The README and the setup guide show how to start.
charles-keys no longer asks for an Anthropic key. A key you added before is simply unused.
The Terms, Privacy Policy and Risk Disclosure now name the seller, Charles LLC, and its address. The Terms are still version 2.0, so there's nothing new to accept.

New Terms of Service and License Agreement (version 2.0), with a Privacy Policy and a Risk Disclosure. They're on charles-bot.xyz and in your Charles folder (LICENSE.md, PRIVACY.md, RISK.md). Run charles-terms to read and accept it.
If you trade real money: live trading waits until you accept version 2.0 (charles-terms). Paper trading carries on as before.
Settings has a Legal section with all three documents, and the steps to trade real money link the Risk Disclosure.
The chat says plainly that its answers aren't investment advice and can be wrong.
The installer shows the new Terms' short version and links the Risk Disclosure and the Privacy Policy.
Fixed: when Coinbase misses a coin's price, the crypto book waits up to 6 hours for it instead of trading without it, and never counts that coin as $0.
Fixed: weekly and monthly reports show the account's real dollar change. What sales made has its own line.
Fixed: reports compare Charles with SPY over the same days. A report no longer shows a Sharpe ratio under 15 market days, and says "Sales: none" when nothing was sold.
The daily loss limit pausing buys is a plain note now, not a warning: it's the safety rule working.
Fixed: the Kalshi page loads quickly again.
Fixed: the chat keeps going when Anthropic hands a question to a backup model, and counts every part toward your monthly cap.
Fixed: charles-copy works when your plan has your own tickers or coins. The copy replaces them, as on the dashboard.
Light mode is greyer on every page, the Kalshi page too.
A moon in the header switches between light and dark in one tap. Settings still has Light, Dark and Match device.
Fixed: charts no longer run back over themselves where hourly points meet midnight.
The Kalshi page drops the note under Charles vs Evil Charles.
Kalshi's open bets each show what they win, and the line under them explains contracts plainly.
Crypto gets everything the stock plan has: presets (Default plan, 0.5× aggressive, 2× aggressive) and your own saved ones, and an Invested slider. The rest of the book waits in cash.
Crypto "My own": search Coinbase's coins and put them in long-term, trend or momentum blocks. Momentum holds the strongest of a block over 90 days, if they're above their trend line.
A saved crypto change trades within the hour, and a coin you take out of your plan is sold.
"Test it on past prices" works for crypto too.
Crypto has a Self-Tune tab: its monthly check tests small changes on Coinbase's prices since 2017. While self-tune is on, one passing change a quarter is made by itself, and it can be undone.
Your own coins aren't shared on the leaderboard. Copying someone goes back to Charles's coins, and Undo brings yours back.
Light mode is a little greyer on every page, the Kalshi page too, and muted text is a touch darker so it stays easy to read.
A new look: one clean typeface, calmer cards, and a soft grey light mode (Dark and Match device are in Settings).
Your own plan: on the Plan tab, search any ticker Alpaca trades and put it in a long-term, sector or momentum block, with how much goes in each. Charles's own plan stays the default.
Presets: Default plan, 0.5× aggressive and 2× aggressive change only the amounts, never the tickers. Save and name your own.
Invested: choose how much of your buying power the plan uses; the rest sits in T-bills.
Self-tune has an on/off switch on the Self-Tune tab. While it's on, a change that passed every test of the monthly evaluation can be applied, at most one a quarter, and you can undo it.

Live trading for stocks, off by default and locked behind steps: charles-live on asks that you're 18 or older, accept the License Agreement, add your own live Alpaca keys and type LIVE. Crypto and Kalshi stay practice money.
The Charles License Agreement: the installer asks you to accept it before installing anything (charles-terms shows it).
A plan with your own tickers or money kept aside isn't shared on the leaderboard.

Kalshi: every bet must stand to win at least half of what it costs, fees included (at most about 67 cents a contract). Evil Charles now skips the other side of a bet when that side would pay less, and so does your account when it copies him.
Kalshi: Charles and Evil Charles place the same bets. Charles bets only where Evil Charles can take the other side and still win at least half his stake.
Kalshi: the graph always spans at least $250 top to bottom, so a small dip no longer fills the whole chart, and the end of the line shows its amount.
Kalshi: a copied bet now costs exactly what the bet it copies cost, using part-contracts in the practice books, so Charles, Evil Charles and your account match to the cent until bets finish.
Kalshi: bets count at what they cost. A $20 bet takes $20 off your account, and a win puts back the stake plus the profit.
Kalshi: when Evil Charles takes the other side, he spends as close to Charles's stake as whole contracts allow, so both bots' values match until bets finish.
Kalshi: each part of the graph's line is blue or red by whose bet moved it. A win from a Charles bet rises in blue even while you follow Evil Charles.
Kalshi: the graph starts at your $1,000, and the win rate counts bets won out of bets finished.
Kalshi: Charles and Evil Charles now both bet on every scan, each with its own practice $1,000, so each builds its own record.
Kalshi: your account follows the bot you pick. One graph shows your account, blue while it follows Charles and red while it follows Evil Charles.
Kalshi: strategies bet from the first scan, with no waiting period. The weather minimum edge is back to 7c.
The tour, now with Charles talking you through Home and the Leaderboard, starts by itself only on a new install. Settings can replay it.
Leaderboard: a Reset button, and a new install's first day says when its chart starts.
Plan vs SPY is measured at the same market close everywhere, so after-hours prices no longer skew it.
Alerts show the whole message when opened, and old or false alarms clear themselves.
The first official release. From here on, updates and Restore work by version.
New dashboard: one Home for every bot, with sliders and Copy on the Plan tab, a side feed, alerts and a short tour.
The dashboard is private with a one-time login link, served over HTTPS on a fresh install.
Pause and Resume, the leaderboard and monthly challenges, and an optional chat on your own Anthropic key.
A new install runs stocks only. Crypto and Kalshi are add-ons.
Notices now appear on the dashboard.
